## Juniper — Junos (SRX, MX, EX/QFX)


### Juniper Junos (SRX, MX, EX/QFX)

```
configure
set system host-name SRX1
set system services ssh root-login deny
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 203.0.113.2/30
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.0.1/24
set routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop 203.0.113.1
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0 host-inbound-traffic system-services ike
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0 host-inbound-traffic system-services ping
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0 host-inbound-traffic system-services ssh
set security address-book global address LAN-NET 10.0.0.0/24
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy ALLOW-WEB match source-address LAN-NET destination-address any application [ junos-http junos-https junos-dns-udp ]
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy ALLOW-WEB then permit
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy ALLOW-WEB then log session-close
set security nat source rule-set T2U from zone trust
set security nat source rule-set T2U to zone untrust
set security nat source rule-set T2U rule R1 match source-address 10.0.0.0/24
set security nat source rule-set T2U rule R1 then source-nat interface
## OSPF / BGP
set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/1.0 passive
set protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/2.0
set policy-options policy-statement EXPORT-BGP term 1 from route-filter 198.51.100.0/24 exact
set policy-options policy-statement EXPORT-BGP term 1 then accept
set protocols bgp group ISP type external peer-as 65000 neighbor 203.0.113.1
set protocols bgp group ISP export EXPORT-BGP
set routing-options autonomous-system 65001
commit check
commit confirmed 5
commit
```
EX/QFX (ELS) switching: `set vlans USERS vlan-id 10`, `set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family ethernet-switching interface-mode access vlan members USERS`,
trunk `interface-mode trunk vlan members [ USERS VOICE ]`, L3 `set interfaces irb unit 10 family inet address 10.0.10.1/24` + `set vlans USERS l3-interface irb.10`.
Advertising a prefix you own: anchor it with `set routing-options static route 198.51.100.0/24 discard` and match
`protocol static` in the export policy. **Never** add `no-readvertise` to that route — it makes it ineligible for export.
Always pair EBGP with explicit import and export policies, plus `family inet unicast accepted-prefix-limit maximum <n> teardown`.
`host-inbound-traffic` set on an interface overrides the zone's setting for that category (`system-services` or `protocols`),
so check where SSH is allowed before adding anything at interface level, or you can drop your own remote session.
`rollback 1` after a confirmed commit restores the *previous* commit (often the new config itself) — check `show system commit` and pick the right number.
Route-based VPN: `security ike proposal/policy/gateway`, `security ipsec proposal/policy/vpn ... bind-interface st0.0`, put `st0.0` in a zone, route to `st0.0`.

Show: `show interfaces terse`, `show route`, `show ospf neighbor`, `show bgp summary`,
`show route advertising-protocol bgp 203.0.113.1`, `show security flow session source-prefix 10.0.0.5`,
`show security policies hit-count`, `show security match-policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust source-ip 10.0.0.5 destination-ip 8.8.8.8 protocol tcp source-port 1024 destination-port 443`,
`show security ike security-associations`, `show security ipsec security-associations`, `monitor traffic interface ge-0/0/1`,
`show | compare`, `show configuration | display set`, `rollback 1` then `commit`.


<!-- references/migration-guide.md -->
## Cross-vendor migration guide


### Cross-vendor migration (e.g. Cisco ASA → FortiGate, Cisco → Palo Alto)

Approach:
1. **Inventory** the source: interfaces/zones, routes, objects, groups, services, ACL/policies, NAT, VPNs, users/auth, HA. Count them so nothing is silently dropped.
2. **Map concepts** (concept map in SKILL.md). Key gotchas:
   - ASA security-levels allow high→low implicitly; the target (FortiGate/PAN/SRX) denies by default → create explicit outbound policies.
   - ASA ACLs use real IPs; FortiGate inbound policies use the **VIP object** as dstaddr; PAN-OS rules use **pre-NAT IP + post-NAT zone**; Junos policies use real IPs (destination NAT happens before policy).
   - Cisco IOS ACLs use **wildcard masks** (`0.0.0.255`) — convert to subnet masks/prefixes.
   - Interface ACLs (per interface, per direction) become zone/interface-pair policies; one ACL may split into several policies.
   - Service names differ (`eq www` → `HTTP`, `https` → `HTTPS`/`service-https`/`junos-https`); define custom services for the rest.
   - Object name rules: avoid spaces/special characters; FortiGate names are max 79 chars, quote names with spaces.
   - Policy-based (crypto map) VPN → route-based on the target is usually preferable; proxy-IDs/selectors must match the peer exactly.
   - Twice/identity NAT for VPN traffic (ASA) → on FortiGate simply leave NAT disabled on the VPN policy.
   - ASA object static NAT (`nat (dmz,outside) static 203.0.113.3`) → FortiGate static-NAT VIP (no portforward); outbound SNAT to the public IP happens automatically on NAT-enabled policies via extintf (see `fortigate.md`, VIP behaviour). ASA `static interface service ...` → port-forward VIP on the interface IP.
   - An interface with an ASA ACL applied loses its security-level implicit permits; interfaces with **no** ACL keep them — convert both cases explicitly (e.g. inside→outside and inside→dmz).
   - Always include pre-checks (central NAT off, interfaces free of default switch/zone membership), a backup command and a rollback/cutback plan (move cables back, clear ARP on the ISP router).
3. **Output** the converted config grouped in dependency order (interfaces → zones → objects → services → routes → NAT/VIPs → policies → VPN), plus a **mapping table** (source line → target object/policy) and a list of items that could not be converted automatically (e.g. inspection/`policy-map`, AAA, ASA-specific features) for manual review.
4. Recommend testing in a lab/maintenance window, and verifying hit counts after cutover.
   Mention vendor tools where relevant: FortiConverter (Fortinet), Cisco FMT (Firewall Migration Tool, ASA→FTD). Palo Alto Expedition is end-of-life (unsupported since January 2025) — migrations to PAN-OS go through Palo Alto Professional Services / partners, cleanup features are moving into Strata Cloud Manager.


<!-- references/mikrotik.md -->
## MikroTik — RouterOS v7


### MikroTik RouterOS (v7; note v6 differences)

Default filter policy is **accept** – always build an explicit firewall. Use Safe Mode (Ctrl+X) when remote. It rolls back if the session drops (after a lost TCP connection this can take up to ~9 minutes), but if a very large change fills its history buffer, Safe Mode exits and the protection is gone — split big changes into smaller Safe Mode sessions, or use a scheduler-based rollback.
Avoid `/system reset-configuration` unless asked — build the VLAN design incrementally: keep the port you're managed through on its current untagged VLAN until you've moved to a new access port, then convert it.
Adding the port you're connected through to a bridge (or changing its PVID) drops that session — do it in its own step, or paste from an `.rsc` file with `/import`, so the rest of the script isn't cut off.
Rule order is top-down: put guest/isolation drops **above** generic accepts (e.g. `accept protocol=icmp`) or they never apply.
In bridge VLAN entries, include the bridge itself as `tagged` for any VLAN that has a `/interface vlan` L3 interface.
Guest isolation from router management also needs `/tool mac-server set allowed-interface-list=LAN`, `/tool mac-server mac-winbox set allowed-interface-list=LAN`, `/ip neighbor discovery-settings set discover-interface-list=LAN`, and IPv6 input rules if IPv6 is enabled.
```
/system identity set name=R1
/ip address add address=203.0.113.2/30 interface=ether1
/ip address add address=10.0.0.1/24 interface=bridge1
/ip route add dst-address=0.0.0.0/0 gateway=203.0.113.1
/ip dns set servers=1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8 allow-remote-requests=yes
/interface list add name=WAN
/interface list add name=LAN
/interface list member add list=WAN interface=ether1
/interface list member add list=LAN interface=bridge1
/ip firewall filter
add chain=input action=accept connection-state=established,related,untracked
add chain=input action=drop connection-state=invalid
add chain=input action=accept protocol=icmp
add chain=input action=accept in-interface-list=LAN
add chain=input action=drop comment="drop all else to router"
add chain=forward action=fasttrack-connection connection-state=established,related hw-offload=yes
add chain=forward action=accept connection-state=established,related,untracked
add chain=forward action=drop connection-state=invalid
add chain=forward action=drop in-interface-list=WAN connection-nat-state=!dstnat
/ip firewall nat
add chain=srcnat out-interface-list=WAN action=masquerade
add chain=dstnat in-interface-list=WAN protocol=tcp dst-port=443 action=dst-nat to-addresses=10.0.0.10 to-ports=443
/ip service disable telnet,ftp,www,api
/ip service set ssh address=10.0.0.0/24
/ip service set winbox address=10.0.0.0/24
```
VLANs (bridge VLAN filtering — enable `vlan-filtering=yes` **last** or you may lose access):
```
/interface bridge add name=bridge1
/interface bridge port add bridge=bridge1 interface=ether2 pvid=10
/interface bridge port add bridge=bridge1 interface=ether5
/interface bridge vlan add bridge=bridge1 vlan-ids=10 tagged=bridge1,ether5 untagged=ether2
/interface vlan add name=vlan10 interface=bridge1 vlan-id=10
/ip address add address=10.0.10.1/24 interface=vlan10
/interface bridge set bridge1 vlan-filtering=yes
```
OSPF v7: `/routing ospf instance add name=default router-id=1.1.1.1` → `/routing ospf area add name=backbone area-id=0.0.0.0 instance=default` → `/routing ospf interface-template add area=backbone networks=10.0.0.0/24`.
BGP v7 (7.1–7.19): `/routing bgp connection add name=ISP as=65001 remote.address=203.0.113.1 remote.as=65000 local.role=ebgp output.network=BGP-OUT` + `/ip firewall address-list add list=BGP-OUT address=198.51.100.0/24`.
RouterOS **7.20+** adds instances: `/routing bgp instance add name=default as=65001 router-id=1.1.1.1` then `/routing bgp connection add name=ISP instance=default remote.address=203.0.113.1 remote.as=65000 local.role=ebgp output.network=BGP-OUT` (`remote.as` is optional — learned from the peer). Check the version with `/system resource print`.
(v6 used `/routing ospf network` and `/routing bgp peer` — different syntax.)
IPsec: `/ip ipsec profile`, `/ip ipsec peer`, `/ip ipsec identity`, `/ip ipsec proposal`, `/ip ipsec policy`; WireGuard: `/interface wireguard` + `/interface wireguard peers`.
Show: `/interface print`, `/ip route print`, `/ip firewall filter print stats`, `/ip firewall connection print where src-address~"10.0.0.5"`,
`/tool ping`, `/tool traceroute`, `/tool sniffer quick ip-address=10.0.0.5`, `/routing ospf neighbor print`, `/routing bgp session print`, `/log print`.
Backup: `/export file=pre-change` (text) and `/system backup save name=pre-change` (binary, same model).


<!-- references/others.md -->
## SonicWall, VyOS/EdgeOS, pfSense/OPNsense, Sophos, UniFi


### Others (brief)

- **SonicWall (SonicOS 7):** primarily GUI (Objects → Address Objects; Policy → Rules and Policies → Access Rules / NAT Rules; Network → IPsec VPN). SonicOS 7 has a CLI with `configure` and `commit`, but syntax varies by firmware — give GUI steps and say to verify CLI with `?`. Troubleshoot: Packet Monitor, Connections Monitor, `diag` pages.
- **VyOS / Ubiquiti EdgeOS:** `configure` → `set interfaces ethernet eth0 address 203.0.113.2/30` → `set protocols static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop 203.0.113.1` → NAT `set nat source rule 100 outbound-interface name eth0` (VyOS 1.4; 1.3/EdgeOS: `outbound-interface eth0`) `source address 10.0.0.0/24` `translation address masquerade` → `commit` → `save`. VyOS 1.4 firewall moved to `set firewall ipv4 forward filter rule ...`; EdgeOS/VyOS 1.3 use named rulesets applied to interfaces. Safety: `commit-confirm 5` then `confirm` within 5 minutes.
- **pfSense / OPNsense:** GUI-driven (Firewall → Rules per interface, first match wins, inbound on the interface the traffic enters; Firewall → NAT → Port Forward/Outbound). Config is `/conf/config.xml`. Shell diagnostics: `pfctl -sr` (rules), `pfctl -ss` (states), `tcpdump -ni em0 host 10.0.0.5`. Backup: Diagnostics → Backup & Restore.
- **Sophos Firewall (SFOS):** GUI/API for rules & NAT (since v18 NAT rules are separate from firewall rules); console has `system diagnostics` and `tcpdump 'host 10.0.0.5'`, `conntrack -L`.
- **Ubiquiti UniFi:** controller-managed; give UI steps, not CLI.


<!-- references/paloalto.md -->
## Palo Alto Networks — PAN-OS


### Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (set format)

Changes go to candidate config; nothing is live until `commit`. Security rules use **pre-NAT IP
and post-NAT zone**.
```
configure
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/1 layer3 ip 203.0.113.2/30
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/2 layer3 ip 10.0.0.1/24
set network interface ethernet ethernet1/2 layer3 interface-management-profile ALLOW-PING
set zone untrust network layer3 ethernet1/1
set zone trust network layer3 ethernet1/2
set network virtual-router default interface [ ethernet1/1 ethernet1/2 ]
set network virtual-router default routing-table ip static-route DEFAULT destination 0.0.0.0/0 nexthop ip-address 203.0.113.1
set address LAN-NET ip-netmask 10.0.0.0/24
set address WEB-SRV ip-netmask 10.0.0.10/32
set rulebase security rules Trust-to-Internet from trust to untrust source LAN-NET destination any application [ web-browsing ssl dns ] service application-default action allow
set rulebase security rules Trust-to-Internet profile-setting group default
set rulebase nat rules SNAT-Internet from trust to untrust source LAN-NET destination any service any source-translation dynamic-ip-and-port interface-address interface ethernet1/1
## Inbound DNAT: NAT rule uses public IP, zone untrust->untrust
set rulebase nat rules DNAT-Web from untrust to untrust destination 203.0.113.2 service service-https destination-translation translated-address WEB-SRV
set rulebase security rules Inbound-Web from untrust to trust destination 203.0.113.2 application ssl service application-default action allow
validate full
commit
```
With the Advanced Routing Engine (PAN-OS 10.2+ when enabled — switching engines needs a commit **and a reboot**)
routing lives under `network logical-router <name> vrf default ...` instead of `virtual-router`. Panorama-managed firewalls: push via device-group/template, don't edit locally.
New boxes often ship with a `default-vwire` on ethernet1/1–1/2: check with `show network virtual-wire` in **configure** mode (op mode: `show virtual-wire all`) and delete it before making those interfaces layer3.
U-turn (internal users → public IP of an internal server): NAT rule from trust to untrust, destination public IP, DNAT to the server **and** SNAT to the trust interface IP; place it above the outbound SNAT rule; security rule is trust→trust to the public IP.

Troubleshoot (operational mode): `show interface all`, `show routing route`, `show session all filter source 10.0.0.5`,
`test security-policy-match from trust to untrust source 10.0.0.5 destination 8.8.8.8 protocol 6 destination-port 443`,
`test nat-policy-match ...`, `show vpn ike-sa`, `show vpn ipsec-sa`, `test vpn ike-sa gateway GW`,
`show counter global filter delta yes severity drop`, `debug dataplane packet-diag ...`, `show high-availability state`, `show system info`.
Rollback: `revert config` (discard candidate) or `load config version <n>` then commit.


<!-- references/sanitizing-configs.md -->
## Sanitizing configs before sharing


Use this when the user is about to paste a config or output, or already pasted one containing secrets.

### What to do when a config with secrets is pasted

- Don't repeat secrets back in your answer; refer to them as `<redacted>` or by their line.
- Tell the user once, briefly, which secrets were exposed and which must be **rotated**, not just
  redacted: anything **reversible** — Cisco `password 7`, Juniper `$9$`, plain-text keys/PSKs,
  SNMP communities — is as good as plain text. Hashed secrets (Cisco `secret 8/9`, Junos `$6$`)
  are lower risk but still worth removing before sharing publicly.
- Keep working on the task; don't refuse because secrets were present.

### How to redact (guidance to give the user)

Goal: remove secrets and identifying details **while keeping every relationship the diagnosis
depends on** — object names, interface names, which rule references which object, subnet sizes,
and which addresses are the same as each other.

1. **Replace, don't delete.** Keep the line, swap the value: `pre-shared-key <PSK-1>`. Deleting
   lines hides structure the diagnosis needs.
2. **Be consistent.** The same secret or address gets the same token everywhere
   (`<PSK-1>`, `PUBLIC-IP-1`), so matching values still match.
3. **Keep subnet sizes and RFC 1918 ranges.** Private addresses usually need no redaction. For
   public IPs, map each to a documentation address (`203.0.113.x`, `198.51.100.x`) and keep the
   prefix length.
4. **Keep names unless they are sensitive.** Hostnames, usernames, customer or site names can
   become `SITE-A`, `USER-1` — consistently.

### Where secrets hide, per vendor

| Vendor | Look for |
|---|---|
| Cisco IOS/NX-OS | `enable secret`, `enable password`, `username ... secret/password`, `password 7 ...`, `key-string`, `pre-shared-key`, `crypto isakmp key`, `snmp-server community`, `tacacs-server key` / `key` under `tacacs server`, `radius-server key`, `ntp authentication-key`, `ip ospf message-digest-key`, BGP `neighbor ... password`, `crypto pki certificate` blocks |
| Cisco ASA | `enable password`, `username ... password`, `ikev1/ikev2 pre-shared-key`, `snmp-server host ... community`, `aaa-server ... key`, certificates and `crypto ca` blocks |
| FortiGate | Every `ENC ...` value (`set password ENC`, `set psksecret ENC`, `set passwd ENC`), `set community`, private keys under `config vpn certificate local`, `set private-key` |
| Palo Alto | `<phash>`, `<key>`, `pre-shared-key`, `<private-key>`, API keys, SNMP `community` |
| Juniper Junos | `encrypted-password`, `$9$...` (reversible), `authentication-key`, `pre-shared-key`, `secret`, `community`, `load-key-file` content |
| MikroTik | `/export` hides most secrets by default; `/export show-sensitive` includes them — share the plain `/export`. Watch `/interface wireguard` private keys and `/ppp secret` if shown |
| Huawei | `cipher` / `irreversible-cipher` values, `pre-shared-key`, `snmp-agent community`, `radius-server shared-key` |
| Linux | Private keys, `.env` files, cloud credentials in scripts; nft/iptables rules are usually safe |
| Cloud | Access keys, secrets in Terraform state or user-data |

### Safe ways to get configs

- Cisco: `show running-config` masks some secrets by type but not `password 7` — redact anyway.
- FortiGate: `show` output contains `ENC` blobs; they are encrypted but tied to the device key —
  still remove them before sharing publicly.
- MikroTik: plain `/export` (without `show-sensitive`).
- Junos: `show configuration | display set` then redact; or share only the hierarchy needed
  (`show configuration security policies`).
- Share only the sections the question needs (the relevant interfaces, policies, NAT, routes).
